note: The catalogue. One row per lesson; the lesson itself is lessons/<id>.json and is fetched only when opened. Groups are drawn in this order, and lessons within a group in this order — they are the shelf's fallback listing when the library fails to load. Each lesson's 'family' is the exact family name in openings/library.json it appears under as the guided entry — hand-mapped, and openings-check asserts the family exists. scripts/openings-check.js validates every file against the shipping chess.js.

groups.name: Open games
groups.blurb: What happens after 1.e4 e5, and the oldest arguments in chess.

groups.name: Semi-open games
groups.blurb: Black answers 1.e4 with something other than 1...e5.

groups.name: Closed games
groups.blurb: 1.d4, and the slower fight for the centre.

groups.name: Indian defences
groups.blurb: 1.d4 Nf6: Black holds the centre pawns back and fights for e4 with pieces.

groups.name: Flank openings
groups.blurb: White keeps the centre pawns home and attacks the centre from the side.

lessons.name: The Italian Game
lessons.blurb: The oldest opening still played at every level: bishop to c4, pointed at f7.

lessons.name: The Ruy Lopez
lessons.blurb: The Spanish bishop on b5: pressure on the knight that defends e5, kept up for forty moves.

lessons.name: The Scotch Game
lessons.blurb: Open the centre on move three and make Black solve it at once.

lessons.name: The Vienna Game
lessons.blurb: Knight before bishop, so that f4 comes with a pawn behind it: the King's Gambit with the risk taken out.

lessons.name: The King's Gambit
lessons.blurb: Give a pawn on move two for the centre and the f-file, and accept that your king will never be entirely safe.

lessons.name: Petrov's Defence
lessons.blurb: Do not defend e5 — attack e4 instead, and take the fight out of 1.e4 e5.

lessons.name: The Sicilian Defence
lessons.blurb: Answer 1.e4 with 1...c5 and refuse the symmetry: a wing pawn for a centre pawn, and a game where Black plays to win.

lessons.name: The French Defence
lessons.blurb: Answer 1.e4 with 1...e6 and 2...d5: a pawn chain, a bad bishop, and a counter-attack that arrives on move three.

lessons.name: The Caro-Kann Defence
lessons.blurb: Answer 1.e4 with 1...c6 and get the solid centre the French wants, without burying the bishop.

lessons.name: The Scandinavian Defence
lessons.blurb: Hit e4 on move one, bring the queen out early, and have the whole opening learned by lunchtime.

lessons.name: The Pirc Defence
lessons.blurb: Let White have the centre, fianchetto, and then attack the centre with pieces from a distance.

lessons.name: Alekhine's Defence
lessons.blurb: Put a knight on f6 and invite the pawns to chase it, on the theory that pawns that have advanced can be attacked.

lessons.name: The Queen's Gambit
lessons.blurb: Offer a pawn you are not really giving away, to trade a wing pawn for the centre.

lessons.name: The Slav Defence
lessons.blurb: Decline the Queen's Gambit with 2...c6 instead of 2...e6, and keep the bishop the Declined gives up.

lessons.name: The London System
lessons.blurb: One setup against everything: d4, Bf4, e3, and a game you understand before it starts.

lessons.name: The Dutch Defence
lessons.blurb: Answer 1.d4 with 1...f5, take e4 away for good, and play for a kingside attack from move one.

lessons.name: The King's Indian Defence
lessons.blurb: Give White the centre, fianchetto, castle — and then throw every kingside pawn at the king.

lessons.name: The Nimzo-Indian Defence
lessons.blurb: Pin the knight on c3, offer to give up the bishop for it, and fight over one square for the rest of the game.

lessons.name: The Grünfeld Defence
lessons.blurb: Fianchetto, then strike with ...d5 on move three: give White a huge centre and spend the whole game attacking it.

lessons.name: The Queen's Indian Defence
lessons.blurb: When White avoids the Nimzo with 3.Nf3, put the bishop on b7 instead and control e4 from the corner.

lessons.name: The Catalan Opening
lessons.blurb: The Queen's Gambit with a bishop on g2: pressure down the long diagonal that lasts the whole game.

lessons.name: The English Opening
lessons.blurb: Start with the c-pawn: a Sicilian with the colours reversed and a move in hand.

lessons.name: The Réti Opening
lessons.blurb: Knight first, then c4 against the d5 pawn: control the centre from a distance before occupying it.
